Rousettus.structure: paired broadband tongue clicks, a few hundred microseconds long
Rousettus.reason: The one pteropodid genus known to echolocate. The clicks are made with the tongue, not the larynx, so this is an independent origin of echolocation rather than an inheritance from the other bats. Because the signal is a broadband click, a peak-frequency range describes it poorly and is not comparable with the peak frequency of a laryngeal call.
warnings: Clicks are broadband, so a peak-frequency range describes them poorly and is not comparable with a laryngeal call.
This genus's range spans 6x, so it does not usefully constrain any individual species.
The genus range itself is poorly constrained.

facts.label: End frequency
facts.ambiguity: Same threshold dependence as start_frequency. facts.label: Peak frequency

facts.label: Start frequency
facts.ambiguity: Threshold-dependent: where the sweep is judged to begin varies with the dB threshold used, which is often unstated. Sources that print 'highest frequency' or 'Fmax' usually mean this for a downward FM sweep, but those headings are registered to max_frequency because they are literal; map them by hand per source rather than by alias.

facts.label: Pulse duration
facts.ambiguity: Threshold-dependent. Values measured from a spectrogram at an unstated dB threshold can differ by a factor of two from envelope-based measures.

alternatives.note: Measurement threshold not stated; not safely comparable with Seibert 2015.

facts.label: Source level
facts.ambiguity: Meaningless without a reference distance (10 cm and 1 m are both in use - a 20 dB difference) and without stating whether the value is rms or peak-equivalent. Both belong in the method record; a source level lacking a stated reference distance must be flagged.
facts.note: dB peSPL at 10 cm from the bat's mouth. Only type 1 calls were analysed, because 92% of moth detection distances were in response to this type. Compare Nyctalus leisleri at 127 dB peSPL under the same method.

facts.label: Source level

facts.note: Absolute source level, dB SPL rms re 20 uPa at 1 m. Apparent source level reported separately as 79.9 ± 5.1.

facts.label: Moth detection distance
facts.ambiguity: Depends on the moth species, which auditory cell (A1 or A2) is used as the criterion, and the assumed hearing threshold. Record the criterion in notes; values using different criteria are not comparable.
facts.note: Field-measured distance at which the A1 auditory cell of the moth Noctua pronuba responds to the approaching bat. Nyctalus leisleri under the same criterion: 33.2 m. value_min/value_max are quartiles, not a range. Modelled prediction was 4.3 m [3.4-6.1 m].

THE HIGHEST-FREQUENCY SPECIES IN THE ENTIRE FRENCH GUIANA FAUNA. Initial frequency can reach 250 kHz; FME averages above 150 kHz and can reach 220 kHz. Bandwidth 75.5 +/- 20.2 kHz. CRITICAL DETECTABILITY NOTE: the extreme frequency gives very low intensity - in a roost the authors could only hear individuals on heterodyne at UNDER 2 METRES. Foraging in the open they are somewhat louder (FME ~200 kHz on approach, ~150 kHz in cruise). Also observed producing audible wing-rustling sounds by rubbing the wings together, possibly social communication compensating for vocal folds specialised on high frequencies unsuited to long-range communication.

Four Anabat/Analook parameters: Dur (duration), Fk (frequency of the knee), Fmin (minimum frequency), Fc (frequency of the flattest part of the call, i.e. characteristic frequency). facts.note: Imported from MASTER_call_records.csv record BAT00240; upload archive sha256 17ffdda2ba6929d03dabcce39119e90d4ee10712fdf690885b3d4a5128d3e464. Monadjem, Shapiro, Mtsetfwa, Reside & McCleery 2017, Acta Chiropterologica 19(1):175-187 (open access via BioOne, full text incl. Table 1 fetched). 178 calls, 145 hand-released individuals, north-eastern Swaziland savanna, 2005-2016. Four Anabat/Analook parameters: Dur (duration), Fk (frequency of the knee), Fmin (minimum frequency), Fc (frequency of the flattest part of the call, i.e. characteristic frequency). Two species attempted but yielded only indistinguishable noise (Nycteris thebaica, Kerivoula lanosa) - both explicitly excluded, not silently missing. Correction factor = 59.68 (inverse of detection-volume half-sphere). Strong negative correlation between detection distance and Fk across species (r=-0.77, P<0.01) - lower-frequency callers are detectable much farther away, a real, quantified source of detectability bias directly analogous to findings in Europe, Borneo and Peru batches earlier in this project, now with an actual correction factor a user could apply.

Strong negative correlation between detection distance and Fk across species (r=-0.77, P<0.01) - lower-frequency callers are detectable much farther away, a real, quantified source of detectability bias directly analogous to findings in Europe, Borneo and Peru batches earlier in this project, now with an actual correction factor a user could apply.

Monadjem, Shapiro, Mtsetfwa, Reside & McCleery 2017, Acta Chiropterologica 19(1):175-187 (open access via BioOne, full text incl. Table 1 fetched). 178 calls, 145 hand-released individuals, north-eastern Swaziland savanna, 2005-2016. Four Anabat/Analook parameters: Dur (duration), Fk (frequency of the knee), Fmin (minimum frequency), Fc (frequency of the flattest part of the call, i.e. characteristic frequency). Two species attempted but yielded only indistinguishable noise (Nycteris thebaica, Kerivoula lanosa) - both explicitly excluded, not silently missing. Correction factor = 0.0002387 (inverse of detection-volume half-sphere). Strong negative correlation between detection distance and Fk across species (r=-0.77, P<0.01) - lower-frequency callers are detectable much farther away, a real, quantified source of detectability bias directly analogous to findings in Europe, Borneo and Peru batches earlier in this project, now with an actual correction factor a user could apply.

Barataud, Giosa, Leblanc, Rufray, Disca, Tillon, Delaval, Haquart & Dewynter 2013, 'Identification et ecologie acoustique des chiropteres de Guyane francaise', Le Rhinolophe 19:103-145. OPEN PDF on the authors' own site, FULL TEXT AND ALL TABLES FETCHED. Time-expansion x10 recordings 2001-2011, Pettersson D1000X/D980/D240X, BatSound analysis. 2526 signals, 379 sequences, 80 species of French Guiana's 103. Method combines AUDITORY analysis (structure, sonority, energy distribution) with computer analysis - the auditory criteria are load-bearing, not decorative. Sonar technology: spatial localisation. FC/total duration ratio 70.1%. Terminal-FC/total-FC ratio 26.7%. FME(FCt) minus terminal frequency = 4.3 kHz (near zero = truly flat FC, required for Doppler; non-zero = sloped). The paper proposes a ~75% FC/total-duration threshold below which Doppler use is compromised.

Monadjem, Shapiro, Mtsetfwa, Reside & McCleery 2017, Acta Chiropterologica 19(1):175-187 (open access via BioOne, full text incl. Table 1 fetched). 178 calls, 145 hand-released individuals, north-eastern Swaziland savanna, 2005-2016. Four Anabat/Analook parameters: Dur (duration), Fk (frequency of the knee), Fmin (minimum frequency), Fc (frequency of the flattest part of the call, i.e. characteristic frequency). Two species attempted but yielded only indistinguishable noise (Nycteris thebaica, Kerivoula lanosa) - both explicitly excluded, not silently missing. Correction factor = 0.0639 (inverse of detection-volume half-sphere). Strong negative correlation between detection distance and Fk across species (r=-0.77, P<0.01) - lower-frequency callers are detectable much farther away, a real, quantified source of detectability bias directly analogous to findings in Europe, Borneo and Peru batches earlier in this project, now with an actual correction factor a user could apply.

Calls of this species exceed the paper's fixed 26 ms analysis window, so this value is measured on a truncated call. Table 1 marks affected values in italics, which are not recoverable from the scanned page; the flag here is applied from the methods statement that Rhinolophidae exceed the window. Applied to duration and minimum frequency only, since truncation removes the end of the call: that shortens the measured duration and raises the measured lowest frequency, while peak and highest frequency sit in the CF portion present from call onset. That last point is our inference from the stated mechanism, not the paper's own marking, and should be checked against a clean copy of the table.

Calls of this species exceed the paper's fixed 26 ms analysis window, so this value is measured on a truncated call. Table 1 marks affected values in italics, which are not recoverable from the scanned page; the flag here is applied from the methods statement that Rhinolophidae exceed the window. Applied to duration and minimum frequency only, since truncation removes the end of the call: that shortens the measured duration and raises the measured lowest frequency, while peak and highest frequency sit in the CF portion present from call onset. That last point is our inference from the stated mechanism, not the paper's own marking, and should be checked against a clean copy of the table.

Table 1 fetched). 178 calls, 145 hand-released individuals, north-eastern Swaziland savanna, 2005-2016. Four Anabat/Analook parameters: Dur (duration), Fk (frequency of the knee), Fmin (minimum frequency), Fc (frequency of the flattest part of the call, i.e. characteristic frequency). Monadjem, Shapiro, Mtsetfwa, Reside & McCleery 2017, Acta Chiropterologica 19(1):175-187 (open access via BioOne, full text incl. Table 1 fetched). 178 calls, 145 hand-released individuals, north-eastern Swaziland savanna, 2005-2016. Four Anabat/Analook parameters: Dur (duration), Fk (frequency of the knee), Fmin (minimum frequency), Fc (frequency of the flattest part of the call, i.e. characteristic frequency). Two species attempted but yielded only indistinguishable noise (Nycteris thebaica, Kerivoula lanosa) - both explicitly excluded, not silently missing. Correction factor = 0.005167 (inverse of detection-volume half-sphere). Strong negative correlation between detection distance and Fk across species (r=-0.77, P<0.01) - lower-frequency callers are detectable much farther away, a real, quantified source of detectability bias directly analogous to findings in Europe, Borneo and Peru batches earlier in this project, now with an actual correction factor a user could apply.

Monadjem, Shapiro, Mtsetfwa, Reside & McCleery 2017, Acta Chiropterologica 19(1):175-187 (open access via BioOne, full text incl. Table 1 fetched). 178 calls, 145 hand-released individuals, north-eastern Swaziland savanna, 2005-2016. Four Anabat/Analook parameters: Dur (duration), Fk (frequency of the knee), Fmin (minimum frequency), Fc (frequency of the flattest part of the call, i.e. characteristic frequency). Two species attempted but yielded only indistinguishable noise (Nycteris thebaica, Kerivoula lanosa) - both explicitly excluded, not silently missing. Correction factor = 0.0002387 (inverse of detection-volume half-sphere). Strong negative correlation between detection distance and Fk across species (r=-0.77, P<0.01) - lower-frequency callers are detectable much farther away, a real, quantified source of detectability bias directly analogous to findings in Europe, Borneo and Peru batches earlier in this project, now with an actual correction factor a user could apply.

facts.note: Imported from MASTER_call_records.csv record BAT02622; upload archive sha256 17ffdda2ba6929d03dabcce39119e90d4ee10712fdf690885b3d4a5128d3e464. [alternation_type=QFC/FMd alternating with pure QFC] | Barataud et al. 2013, Le Rhinolophe 19:103-145 (open PDF, full text fetched). MAJOR EXCEPTION within Phyllostomidae. Uses QFC/FMd structure and alternates narrowband/broadband signals like the Noctilionidae - nothing like its own family. Bandwidth 8.4 kHz (7.1-10.4), FC/total duration 53.9%. A second signal type is pure QFC at 38.4 kHz with ZERO bandwidth and 100% FC ratio. Its frequencies do not overlap any other species with the same structure, so it is EASILY identified acoustically - the single most acoustically distinctive phyllostomid in the fauna. It is also the only one whose FME sits on harmonic 2, which is what separates it from the emballonurids it otherwise mimics.

Monadjem, Shapiro, Mtsetfwa, Reside & McCleery 2017, Acta Chiropterologica 19(1):175-187 (open access via BioOne, full text incl. Table 1 fetched). 178 calls, 145 hand-released individuals, north-eastern Swaziland savanna, 2005-2016. Four Anabat/Analook parameters: Dur (duration), Fk (frequency of the knee), Fmin (minimum frequency), Fc (frequency of the flattest part of the call, i.e. characteristic frequency). Two species attempted but yielded only indistinguishable noise (Nycteris thebaica, Kerivoula lanosa) - both explicitly excluded, not silently missing. Correction factor = 0.0004501 (inverse of detection-volume half-sphere). Strong negative correlation between detection distance and Fk across species (r=-0.77, P<0.01) - lower-frequency callers are detectable much farther away, a real, quantified source of detectability bias directly analogous to findings in Europe, Borneo and Peru batches earlier in this project, now with an actual correction factor a user could apply.
